question: What does the systolic blood pressure reading measure?

options.A: The pressure when the heart rests
options.B: The total volume of blood in the body
options.C: The pressure when the heart beats
options.D: The speed of blood flow in veins

explanation: Systolic pressure represents the force in the arteries when the heart muscle contracts to pump blood forward. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why don't we diagnose someone with high blood pressure (hypertension) after just one high reading?

options.A: Nigerian guidelines require at least five months of tracking
options.B: Blood pressure machines only work accurately on the third try
options.C: Systolic pressure changes constantly based on what food was eaten
options.D: Temporary factors like stress or rushing can falsely raise readings

explanation: Things like rushing to the clinic, traffic anxiety, or pain can make BP jump temporarily. That's why we always check a few times before making a diagnosis. Great job thinking like a nurse!

question: Primary hypertension is also frequently called what?
explanation: We call it 'essential hypertension' when high blood pressure happens on its own without another clear medical condition causing it. Easy peasy!

question: Which of the following is a modifiable risk factor for hypertension?
explanation: Modifiable risk factors are lifestyle habits or conditions that a person can change, such as reducing salt intake, unlike age or genetics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h2)

question: Why is hypertension frequently called the 'silent killer'?

options.A: It usually causes no symptoms in its early stages
options.B: Patients refuse to talk about their diagnosis
options.C: It stops the heart without any warning sounds
options.D: It only affects people who are sleeping

explanation: Because high blood pressure rarely causes physical discomfort initially, individuals often remain unaware of their condition until complications arise. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h3)

question: If a patient has severe hypertension, which symptom might they complain about?

options.A: Severe pain in the lower abdomen

explanation: A pounding headache right at the back of the head (occipital area) when waking up is a classic warning sign of very high pressure. Keep storing these clinical pearls!

question: What happens to a patient's blood pressure reading if you use a cuff that is too small for their arm?

options.A: The blood pressure reading will be falsely low
options.B: The mercury column will fail to rise at all
options.C: The reading will remain completely normal
options.D: The blood pressure reading will be falsely high

explanation: A tiny cuff squeezes too hard against a big arm, making the reading look much higher than it really is. Always match your cuff size to the patient!

question: How long should a patient sit quietly before you measure their blood pressure?
explanation: Giving them 5 minutes to sit and breathe lets walking, talking, or anxiety settle so you get an accurate baseline reading.

question: What is the main goal of the DASH diet for someone with high blood pressure?

options.A: To increase potassium, calcium, and fiber while reducing sodium
options.B: To replace all fluid intake with specialized herbal teas
options.C: To encourage rapid weight loss through strict calorie counting
options.D: To eliminate all carbohydrates from the daily meal plan

explanation: DASH focuses on whole foods packed with good minerals like potassium and calcium while cutting back on salt to protect the heart.

question: Which of these is NOT a good lifestyle change for managing high blood pressure?
explanation: More salt (sodium) holds onto water in the body and pushes blood pressure up—definitely something we want patients to cut back on!

question: A patient says, 'My BP is normal today, so I'll stop my drugs.' What is the best way for a nurse to reply?

options.A: Suggest replacing the prescribed drugs with local palm wine
options.B: Agree that normal readings mean the disease has gone away permanently
options.C: Tell the patient to double the dose whenever they feel dizzy
options.D: Explain that the medication controls the condition rather than curing it

explanation: Normal readings just mean the medication is doing its job! Stopping it will cause the pressure to shoot right back up. Patient education is key!

question: What does the term 'orthostatic hypotension' mean?

options.A: A sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up
options.B: Swelling in the lower legs due to poor circulation
options.C: A spike in heart rate after eating heavy meals
options.D: High blood pressure caused by sleeping flat on the back

explanation: When blood vessels are slow to adjust to a new position, standing up too fast can cause a dizzy spell because of a sudden drop in pressure. Good to know for patient safety!

question: What is the main difference between hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: Whether the patient is male or female
options.B: The time of day the blood pressure was checked
options.C: The exact numerical value of the diastolic reading
options.D: The presence of acute target organ damage

explanation: Urgency means extremely high pressure, but emergency means the high pressure is actively harming vital organs like the heart or brain. Big difference in how fast we act!

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with a BP of 220/130 mmHg, chest pain, and confusion. What are they likely experiencing?
explanation: Extremely high blood pressure plus signs of brain or heart distress (like confusion and chest pain) makes this a critical medical emergency. You're crushing these clinical scenarios!
